title: Rav Natan

paragraphs: Yoma 78a mentions the Exilarch visiting Rav Natan’s house in Hagronya. Rafram and all the other rabbis came to the lecture, but Ravina did not. Hyman finds no other mention of this Rav Natan.
And as for what we find in Beitzah 35b and Nazir 51a, the name Rav Natan should, according to Hyman, read Rav Natan bar Oshaya there.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: Hyman’s statement that this Rav Natan is not found elsewhere is his own survey claim, not a new exhaustive search. במק״א is read in context as “elsewhere.”
The sentence continues across these two units. Hyman proposes the patronymic bar Oshaya for the Beitzah 35b and Nazir 51a mentions; that proposal does not alter the heading or merge the entries.
The references follow the supplied Hebrew: Yoma 78a, Beitzah 35b and Nazir 51a. The supplied proofread text reads Nazir; the historical ניר form belongs to OCR provenance.
